expectations.text: Rejects the 6-month window as below the floor for a fully public API.
expectations.evidence: "6 months is far below the benchmarks for your public audience."

expectations.text: States a floor of at least 12 months of deprecation notice for fully public APIs.
expectations.evidence: "Published floors for public APIs are at least 12 months (Google Cloud, Shopify)."

expectations.text: Raises the recommendation to at least 24 months specifically because Trackpole's consumers ship mobile apps.
expectations.evidence: "The skill's rule for mobile consumers is at least 24 months."

expectations.text: Gives the reason for the 24-month floor: app-store update cycles and end-user update lag are slow and outside the provider's control.
expectations.evidence: "App-store release cycles and users who never update make them the slowest group to migrate."

expectations.text: Does not accept the competitor's 3-month window as a justification or benchmark for the number.
expectations.evidence: "The competitor's 3 months isn't a benchmark."

expectations.text: Replaces the notice period for the 9 internal services with consumer-driven contract testing and coordinated deploys rather than applying the same window to them.
expectations.evidence: "Use coordinated deploys and consumer-driven contract tests instead."

expectations.text: Explains why internal consumers differ: a notice period compensates for being unable to coordinate with consumers directly, and internal teams can coordinate.
expectations.evidence: "The 9 services have owners you can reach." The explanation is brief.
